claims.text: The starting additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy retains an FCC matrix.
The starting alloy has high strength.
The starting alloy has notable fatigue resistance.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by the formation and evolution of a mixed oxide scale.
The integrity of the mixed oxide scale is controlled by synergistic interactions among Cr, Al, and Ti oxide formation.
An oxidizing atmosphere produces a transient protective mixed oxide scale.
The transient scale formed in an oxidizing atmosphere temporarily inhibits further degradation.
The oxide scale is less stable in a reducing atmosphere than in an oxidizing atmosphere.
Reduced scale stability in a reducing atmosphere accelerates the breakdown of surface integrity.
Scale adherence, porosity, and thickness mediate the alloy's degradation.
Reduction of oxide constituents under reducing conditions destabilizes chromium- and titanium-containing oxides.
Destabilization of oxide constituents disrupts scale continuity.
Disruption of scale continuity exposes the underlying alloy and accelerates degradation.
Degradation is largely confined to the surface, thereby preserving the integrity of the FCC matrix during the applicable exposure regime.
Oxidizing exposure will produce a more uniform and adherent scale and slower degradation than reducing exposure.
Reducing exposure will produce more scale spallation or pore formation than oxidizing exposure.
Scale failure under reducing conditions will correlate with greater mechanical degradation than under oxidizing conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies above the temperature needed to activate oxide kinetics but below the temperature for bulk phase transformation.
